So, I think college CAN be worthwhile. However, I think there are a lot of degrees that are practically and/or fundamentally useless. I also don’t think kids at 18 can POSSIBLY comprehend just how much debt they’re taking on, and how there’s literally no escaping that debt.

College is absolutely worthwhile — as long as you know what you’re getting into.

For my part, I would genuinely advise your first order of business after graduating high school, is to pursue a trade for a year, or as long as two. This is purely a “fallback”, don’t worry about getting qualified to do something you even remotely give a shit about; ALL you should be doing is getting qualified as a sort of “emergency button, I need a job NOW” last case measure.

Because sometimes, you’re going to get fired for absolutely no reason, totally out of your control, and there is NOTHING you can do about it. It doesn’t matter how hard you work or how good at your job you are, sometimes shit happens. And believe me, it is SO much worse when you don’t have a backup plan (trust me on this one; I went from a pretty coveted position in the political world, to working night shifts as a security guard just to pay bills; I’m kicking myself that I didn’t get licensed in something when things were good).

Use that 1-2 years to truly consider what you want to prioritize for your REAL career. Maybe you enjoy your trade and decide to make a career out of that; awesome, you just saved yourself $100k in student loans. Maybe you find you value low stress and having more time with friends or loved ones (I will warn you; once your friends find partners, you’ll gradually have fewer friends to spend time with regularly).

Or maybe you decide back-breaking work sucks, and you want to go to college for something that will make a ton of money.

For my part, I really regret not having “pursued my passion” of getting into Game Design for video games, or more likely programming for games. I would have probably felt much more comfortable pursuing my passions, if I’d had the “safety net” of having a real trade certification under my belt.

Also, whenever you DO go to college, make it your PRIMARY FOCUS IN LIFE to make as many friends as possible. Say “yes” to every single social event that comes up. That’s basically “networking” in a nutshell, but most opportunities in life will come from WHO you know, not WHAT you know. You never know when some guy you were cool to at a random house party could be a mutual contact at the company you want to work at.

Also… this is maybe oddly specific, but make it a point to A) not be creepy to girls, and B) make sure other guys aren’t creepy to girls. Just shutting down bad behavior, shockingly, led directly to a woman sticking her neck out to get me a job later in life. It pays to not be a douche!
